question: Asked after two linked-list coding questions in the first technical (screening, about 45 minutes) round for Associate Software Engineer at Qualcomm: **the difference between method overloading and method overriding, the concept of abstraction, and static methods and variables.**
lookingFor: Can you distinguish compile-time from run-time polymorphism precisely?
Do you understand abstraction as hiding implementation behind an interface, not just a keyword?
Do you know what static means for storage and for binding (class-level, no instance needed)?
Do you back each definition with a small example?
followUps: Can a constructor be overloaded? Can it be overridden?
What is the difference between an abstract class and an interface?
Why can a static method not access non-static members directly?
What happens if you call an overridden method from a base-class constructor in C++?
What is function hiding in C++?
